branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Public statements shift from whether to reallocate space to how to mitigate loading and neighborhood parking impacts.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Council moderates gain cover to back a revised but substantial redesign, especially if delivery mitigations are added.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Safety audit finds current corridor design poses meaningful safety or reliability problems and supports lane changes.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Officials increasingly call for phased implementation, pilot language, or further study rather than full approval.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Council delays, narrows, or pilots the plan instead of approving full corridor conversion.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Safety audit is inconclusive or questions benefits relative to disruption.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Joint appearances, shared messaging, or co-signed communications from merchants and neighborhood groups.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: An anti-redesign coalition forms strong enough to sway swing council members toward postponement or substantial rollback.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Petition gains visible signatures and homeowner concerns are publicly linked to business losses.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Media coverage highlights rider and safety testimony at parity with or above parking-loss complaints.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Perceived public support for reallocation rises, reducing council fear of backing visible curb changes.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Transit riders and safety advocates turn out strongly at hearing with credible stories about delays and crashes.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Merchant pragmatists and moderate homeowners publicly distinguish themselves from maximal opponents.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Conflict softens enough for a partial coalition supporting a modified redesign.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Mayor and agency introduce loading zones, timed deliveries, or residential parking management as concessions.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A pilot, delay, or single-corridor compromise would not satisfy this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: Council approves a substantial corridor conversion including bus lanes and protected bike lanes on both corridors, not merely a study or pilot.
endpoint_ledger.label: Full redesign approved

meta.important_question: Will the city council approve a substantial redesign that includes both bus lanes and protected bike lanes on the two corridors?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the clearest terminal version of the proposal implied by the scenario.
realization_criteria: formal council vote passes corridor redesign authorization
approved package includes bus lanes on both targeted corridors
approved package includes protected bike lanes on both targeted corridors
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Proposal is active but no approval has occurred at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A pure deferral or study order without implementation authority would not satisfy this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: Council approves a narrowed, phased, or mitigated redesign rather than the original full conversion.
endpoint_ledger.label: Modified compromise approved

meta.important_question: Will decision-makers converge on a modified package with mitigations or partial implementation rather than the original proposal?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario contains strong incentives for bargaining through mitigations and scope adjustments.
realization_criteria: formal council vote passes a corridor action package
package materially changes original scope through phased rollout, corridor reduction, pilot status, or explicit loading/parking mitigations
decision is framed as implementation rather than indefinite study
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Multiple stakeholder concerns suggest compromise is a live endpoint at initialization.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Short scheduling changes that still culminate in timely approval do not satisfy this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: Formal approval is not achieved within the immediate six-week window and the matter is postponed, sent back for more study, or tabled.
endpoint_ledger.label: Decision delayed or deferred

meta.important_question: Will unresolved audit findings and coalition resistance push the decision into delay, deferral, or further study beyond the six-week window?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Process friction may dominate if legitimacy or vote counts remain weak.
realization_criteria: no formal approval of full or modified redesign by end of the six-week window
official action postpones, tables, studies, or defers the decision
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Unresolved audit and coalition uncertainty make delay a credible terminal option.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Simple parallel complaints without coordinated effect are insufficient.
endpoint_ledger.description: Merchant and homeowner coordination becomes durable enough to force major redesign rollback, significant parking retention, or politically visible retreat.
endpoint_ledger.label: Opposition coalition reshapes outcome

meta.important_question: Will merchant and homeowner opposition consolidate into a durable coalition capable of reshaping council votes?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Coalition durability is central to whether opposition changes the final decision path.
realization_criteria: merchant and homeowner groups engage in sustained joint public or lobbying activity
council or mayor materially revises proposal toward parking retention because of that coalition
official statements cite local business or spillover parking backlash as a decisive reason
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Shared parking-loss concerns create a plausible but not yet fully consolidated coalition at T0.

simulation_brief.summary: A fictional coastal city is considering replacing street parking on two commercial corridors with bus lanes and protected bike lanes following late buses and minor crashes. Transit reliability, street safety, delivery access, neighborhood parking spillover, and near-term council politics are all active pressures. The mayor needs council votes within six weeks. A public hearing is pending, merchants are organizing a petition, and a safety audit remains unresolved.
simulation_brief.time_horizon_note: Near-term policy decision window centered on the next six weeks.
uncertainty_notes: Safety audit findings are unresolved at T0.
Exact council composition and vote commitments are not specified.
Scale of merchant opposition and rider mobilization is plausible but not numerically specified in source.

sociology_baseline.note: Actors are more persuadable by mitigation details than by opposing value frames.
Broader public likely remains inactive unless hearing coverage or parking/safety narratives intensify.
Some private support for redesign is muted by uncertainty and fear of standing out locally.
sociology_baseline.scope: quiet bus supporters and mixed homeowners

sociology_baseline.note: Local peer networks reinforce parking and access concerns.
Visible testimony from multiple constituencies may be needed to normalize support for street reallocation.
Issue interpretation is filtered through livelihood, commuting, and neighborhood identity.
Without catalytic events, broad interest may remain shallow despite stakeholder conflict.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Safety framing has legitimacy potential but is constrained by the unresolved audit.
Repeated late buses create a practical service narrative favoring bus lanes.
Visible parking loss is easier for opponents to organize around than future reliability gains are for supporters.
Homeowner concern is focused on neighborhood externalities rather than corridor-wide transport performance.
Six-week deadline increases bargaining leverage for organized groups and raises value of near-term public events.
